definitions.gloss: decoration; an ornamental addition designed to make something look more festive, attractive, or special; the act of adding such decorations
definitions.explanation: Borrowed from English 'decoration'. Used in Japanese for any added ornamental element placed on cakes, rooms, shop windows, walls, holiday displays, gifts, or personal possessions. Also used as a する-verb (デコレーションする 'to decorate'). It is especially associated with food (デコレーションケーキ 'decorated cake') and with the Japanese subculture of decorating phones, nails, and gadgets with rhinestones and stickers (デコ).

notes:
Borrowed from English 'decoration'. Used as a noun and as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧-verb (デコレーション⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ 'to decorate'). The shortened form デコ exists as a productive prefix in informal Japanese for decorated objects: デコ{弁|べん} ('decorated bento'), デコ{電|でん} ('decorated phone'), デコ{爪|づめ} or デコネイル ('decorated nails').

USAGE:
The word is most commonly used about three things:
- decorated cakes and other foods (especially birthday and Christmas cakes)
- holiday and event decorations for rooms and shops (Christmas, Halloween, weddings, parties)
- decorative items for personal possessions (phone cases, nails, school supplies)

It is broader than the everyday word ⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧ ('ornament'), and tends to feel slightly more deliberate or stylish.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Used as a plain noun and as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧-verb. The patterns ⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧デコレーション⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ and ⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧デコレーション⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ are both common and roughly interchangeable. The use as a な-modifier of a noun is uncommon — instead, use the noun-noun compound デコレーション + N (e.g. デコレーション⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- デコレーション⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to decorate (something)
- デコレーション⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to decorate (verb form)
- デコレーション⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{施|ほどこ}す→施す：12985_hodokosu⟧: to apply decorations (more formal)
- デコレーション⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧: a decorated cake (e.g. a birthday cake with cream and fruit)
- ⟦クリスマス→クリスマス：03839_kurisumasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコレーション: Christmas decorations
- ⟦ハロウィン→ハロウィン：27505_harowin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコレーション: Halloween decorations
- ⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコレーション: room decorations
- ⟦{壁|かべ}→壁：01290_kabe⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコレーション: wall decorations
- ⟦{華|はな}やか→華やか：06070_hanayaka⟧なデコレーション: gorgeous decorations
- ⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧デコレーション: handmade decorations

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧: decoration, ornament — the everyday native word; broader and more neutral. Less stylistically marked than デコレーション.
- ⟦{飾|かざ}り{付|つ}け→飾り付け：17469_kazaritsuke⟧: decoration (especially the act of decorating a place or object) — the native verbal noun; very close to デコレーション in meaning and usage.
- ⟦{装飾|そうしょく}→装飾：14104_soushoku⟧: ornamentation, decoration — a more formal Sino-Japanese word; common in design, architecture, and historical contexts.
- デコ: deco — the abbreviated, casual form, used as a prefix for decorated items (デコ{弁|べん}, デコ{電|でん}, デコ{爪|づめ}).
- デコる: to decorate, to deck out — a colloquial verb derived from デコ; common in youth slang.

CULTURAL NOTE:
A デコレーション⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧ is a key part of Japanese birthday and Christmas celebrations. The classic Japanese Christmas cake is a sponge cake with whipped cream and strawberries. デコ culture — decorating phones, nails, school items, and bento boxes with cute additions — has been a notable part of Japanese youth fashion since the early 2000s.
